newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Ninety-two countries to sign Ottawa landmine ban.
newsitem.headline: Ninety-two countries to sign Ottawa landmine ban.

text.p: Ninety-two countries have signed the Declaration of Brussels preparing a first-ever landmine ban treaty to be signed in Ottawa, Canada in December, diplomats at the Brussels conference told Reuters on Friday.

The organisers of the four-day Conference on a Global Ban on Anti-personnel Mines are due to make a formal statement about the number of countries who have signed the Brussels Declaration at the conference's closing news conference later today.

The signatories include African, central American and some Asian countries as well as all European Union nations with the exception of Greece and Finland. Greece refuses to sign because of territorial disputes with Turkey while Finland refuses because of its long border with Russia.

A total of 115 countries have been taking part in the Brussels talks. Signature of the Brussels Declaration was a precondition for countries to be allowed to join talks in Oslo, Norway, in September where the exact wording of the Ottawa treaty will be negotiated.

The landmine talks, which started in Ottawa at the end of 1996, are set to lead to the signing of the first-ever treaty to ban the production, use, stockpiling and transfer of anti-personnel landmines.
The U.S. which is attending the Brussels conference as an observer only, will not sign because it favours separate United Nations-sponsored landmine talks in Geneva.
Thirty-six other delegations took part in the talks as observers. They included Cuba, Greece, India, Indonesia, Iran, Israel, Libya, Pakistan, the Palestinian Authority and Turkey.
